data.name: Ammaar
data.gender_notes: Ammaar is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who is patient and persevering in the face of adversity, as in the Quranic verse 13:24. The name Ammaar carries the meaning “One who is patient” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Ammaar usually hope their child will grow to embody one who is patient and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: To endure and remain steadfast in the face of challenges, as exemplified by the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)
data.etymology: Ammaar belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “One who is patient.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ammaar total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

in_english.name: Ammaar
in_english.long_meaning: Ammaar is a name that signifies long life and longevity, derived from the Arabic root Amr, which means to live and remain, and is mentioned in the Quran in Surah Al-Baqarah, and is considered important in Islamic tradition and culture

data.cultural_impact: The name "Ammaar" may be of Arabic origin and is widely used within the Islamic community across the globe. It carries an inherent sense of strength and resilience, which aligns well with the values of many Islamic cultural and historical figures. For instance, in Islamic history, there is a famous Islamic scholar named Ibn Ammar Al-Qurashi who was known for his enduring curiosity and love for knowledge.
data.spiritual_significance: Spiritually, the name "Ammaar" holds a deeper meaning inspired by Islamic teachings. The name "Ammaar" can be derived from the Arabic word "amr," meaning command or order. In the context of the Islamic faithful, being a commanded servant of Allah, it has a spiritual significance that all devout Muslims should strive to uphold. The name might serve as a reminder of the spiritual importance of patience and perseverance as exemplified in the Quranic verse, "And [mention, O Muhammad], when Abraham was tried by his Lord with certain commands, he fulfilled them. He it is who said, 'Indeed, I will make you the Imam [leader] of my people after you and increase you greatly.' [So] ask Me not about that which is to come after it." [Surah Al-Baqarah 13:24]. The verse teaches that even in the face of adversity and hardship, we should remain steadfast and faithful to Allah's commands.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The meaning "One who is patient" symbolizes One who is patient and persevering in the face of adversity, as in the Quranic verse 13:24. In Islamic spirituality, bearing the name Ammaar serves as a constant reminder of one's spiritual aspirations and connection to Islamic values of one who is patient.
